solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument is breaking silence soon (8)

indicators.note: HARP IS breaks into SH, splitting it open

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is about to shatter a hush.
explanation.walkthrough: SHARPISH is informal British for 'quickly, soon', as in 'get here sharpish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sharpish means doing it promptly, so soon.

clue.text: Slick soldiers led by sergeant major (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, SM comes first and the soldiers follow

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking troop marching behind their sergeant major.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers are named first but placed second: 'led by' puts the sergeant major in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means unctuously smooth and ingratiating, which is slick in the oily sense.

clue.text: Flower festival’s not starting (5)

indicators.note: the festival loses its opening letter

blocks.note: EASTER without its first letter E

explanation.surface: A flower show that fails to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: The festival is Easter; the 's is just 'is', telling us what the beheaded word becomes.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden flower.

clue.text: Long to fill a jug (7)

indicators.note: ITCH goes inside PER, filling it

blocks.note: a = per, as in 'ten pounds a head'
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Someone yearning to fill up a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to yearn; the small word 'a' carries PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitcher is a large jug with a lip and handle.

clue.text: What features Jack and Tony and Keith? (4,4,2,3)

definitions.text: What features Jack and Tony and Keith?

blocks.note: Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis, stars of a 1959 Billy Wilder comedy
not in the film's cast; the title, read as an instruction to take some of its letters, spells this name

explanation.surface: A question about which show stars three men named Jack, Tony and Keith.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is the wordplay and the clue is its result. Read the title as an instruction, 'some' of 'liKE IT Hot', and it gives KEITH. So the film features Jack and Tony as stars, and Keith inside its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Like It Hot is the Billy Wilder comedy starring Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis.

clue.text: Section of foot marching together (6)

blocks.note: the arched top of the foot

explanation.surface: A unit of infantry marching in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' reads as foot soldiers, infantry, so 'section of foot marching together' looks like a drill order, not anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched middle part of the foot between toes and ankle.

clue.text: “Strange way” — an older equivalent of Strangeways? (7)

blocks.note: a gate is a way in or through

explanation.surface: A quoted phrase that seems to split the name Strangeways in two.
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeways is a Manchester prison and Newgate was a famous old London prison; the clue translates Strange-way into New-gate piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate, closed in 1902, was a notorious London jail, an older counterpart of Strangeways.

clue.text: US drivers pay for these weapons to support revolution (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the weapons sit under TURN, holding it up

explanation.surface: American motorists funding weapons for an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests a political uprising, which the weapons back up; it is a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is an American toll road, which drivers pay to use.

clue.text: Nit-picking editor’s got in store (8)

indicators.note: the editor is taken inside the store

explanation.surface: A fussy editor has something in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': the editor has got in (to) the store.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive attention to minor details, which is nit-picking.

clue.text: What could switch off meters locally in NY cab rank? (9)

indicators.note: 'In' is used literally: the M for meters is placed in the middle of TIER, as a thing is in a box

blocks.note: auto is the American word for a car
a tier is a rank or level
m = meters, the US spelling of metres

explanation.surface: Wondering what might turn off the meters in a New York taxi queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' tells us 'meters' is spelt the New York way; the abbreviation is plain M. A cab rank reads as a taxi queue, but rank is TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An autotimer switches a device off automatically at a set time.

clue.text: US politician admits to including one further release (13)

indicators.note: To admit is to let someone in, so REPUBLICAN lets TIO inside it
Something including another has it as one of its parts, so TO holds I within it

blocks.note: a member of the Republican Party

explanation.surface: An American politician concedes backing another release, perhaps of prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admits' reads as a politician confessing; here it means letting in. 'Release' suggests freeing someone, but it is a published edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Republication is publishing again, a further release of a book or text.

clue.text: Get married, keeping bride’s heart right tense (5)

indicators.note: WED holds the other letters inside
the centre letter of BRIDE

explanation.surface: A wedding where the bride's heart is in the right place, though nerves run high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar, fitting a clue about getting married; it is the adjective, on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Wired, informally, means edgy and highly strung, which is tense.

clue.text: Senior officer notes force returning (7)

indicators.note: the letters come back the other way

blocks.note: lah is a note of the sol-fa scale
to ram something is to force it

explanation.surface: A senior officer's notes about troops coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a noun, an army unit returning, but it is the verb ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal, as in field marshal or air marshal, is a very senior officer.

clue.text: What surrounds newish issue in drama by author? (7)

explanation.surface: A question about what frames a fresh topic in a writer's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring: newish issue is a toddler, whom a playpen surrounds. The clue reads as a literary question.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a portable enclosure that surrounds a small child while it plays.

clue.text: Assault wave, one working during action (13)

blocks.note: a breaker is a wave crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: A soldier joining a wave of assault in the middle of battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' reads as combat, fitting assault and wave; it is industrial action, a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker keeps working, or is hired to work, while others are on strike.

clue.text: Fifty netted by not so common killer (9)

indicators.note: L is caught inside STRANGER

explanation.surface: Fifty caught by a rare murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so common' is a comparative, so it needs a comparative answer: stranger, meaning rarer, not an unknown person.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is someone who kills by throttling.

clue.text: Fortune teller interrupted by Saint David? (8)

indicators.note: An interrupted speaker has something cut into the middle of them, so PALMIST is split open by S

explanation.surface: A palm reader cut off by St David, patron saint of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint David' looks like one name; the saint goes into the wordplay and David alone is the definition, with the question mark marking him as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, so he is the Psalmist.

clue.text: See disruption to travel as resulting from accident (13)

indicators.note: the letters are sent off on a journey, moving about

explanation.surface: A travel update blaming the delays on an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disruption' is so much like an anagram indicator that it seems to act on 'See'; it is fodder itself, and 'to travel' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Serendipitous describes a happy discovery made by chance, so resulting from accident.

clue.text: Very disagreeable row about sovereign’s gift (7)

indicators.note: 'About' in its sense of 'around', so NOISE is wrapped around OM

blocks.note: the Order of Merit, awarded personally by the monarch

explanation.surface: An unpleasant quarrel over something the monarch gave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel; it is a racket. The OM is an honour in the monarch's personal gift, not a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells.

clue.text: Essential points exposed on railway (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, OUT sits on top of LINE

blocks.note: a secret that is out is exposed

explanation.surface: Key points of a railway line left open to the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' on a railway are track switches, so the surface stays on the line; here they are just the main ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outline is a summary giving only the main features of something.

clue.text: Generally tough circling island (6)

indicators.note: To circle something is to go all round it, so MANLY surrounds I

explanation.surface: A general, rugged type sailing round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: MANLY is the less obvious reading of 'tough': rugged, not hard to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly means for the most part, generally.

clue.text: Going on a bit, unfortunately losing height (7)

indicators.note: the letters come out badly, jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone getting older and sadly shrinking a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing height' begs to be read as a deletion of H; both words are fodder instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something longish is fairly long, going on a bit.

clue.text: Girl accepting a number as receiver (7)

indicators.note: Accepting something means taking it in, so ANNA takes TEN inside her

explanation.surface: A girl agreeing to take a phone number as the person answering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a telephone handset, which fits a girl taking a number; it is an aerial.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna receives radio or television signals.

clue.text: Person not turning up without son under any conditions (5)

definitions.note: NOHOW means 'not under any conditions'; the negative is carried by the sentence the answer sits in

indicators.note: 'Without' in its sense of 'lacking', so NO-SHOW carries on without its S

explanation.surface: Someone who never arrives, missing a son, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not turning up' reads as a reversal instruction; it is part of the definition of a no-show.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is dialect for 'in no way', used as in 'I can't do it nohow'.

clue.text: Initially in mostly dark northern home (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'in'
drop the last letter of GLOOM

explanation.surface: Living in near-darkness in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting: an Arctic winter is mostly dark, and the igloo is its home.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit snow house of the far north.

clue.text: Feature of Stonehenge print involving stone covered in star signs regularly missed (9)

indicators.note: LITHO is wrapped in the letters from the star signs
every other letter is skipped

blocks.note: a litho is a lithograph, a print made from a stone

explanation.surface: Describing a Stonehenge print of a stone decorated with zodiac signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving stone' is not an instruction but describes the print: lithography was first done from a flat stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilithon is two upright stones topped by a lintel, the signature structure of Stonehenge.

clue.text: Arranged great time in quarry (6)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Having a great time in a stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' suggests a stone pit; it is the hunted prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarry is what you pursue, your target.

clue.text: Like a moving boat captained by character (5,3)

blocks.note: a crew serves under its captain

explanation.surface: A boat moving off with a real character at the helm.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship is under way once it is moving through the water; the whole clue stays on the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Under way is the nautical term for a vessel in motion.
